summary: Prefix cache revalidation spike causes conversational-turn p99 latency and intermittent 504s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbusChat reports intermittent p99 latency spikes (6-10s) and occasional 504s that correlate to repeated user turns in a multi-turn chat flow. Behavior started after a model variant rollout last week. Impact: production traffic degraded for 2 of their top routes, causing UX timeouts and escalations to their SREs.

Impact:
- Multiple sessions show bursty p99 latency increases from ~400ms baseline to 6-10s for 30-90s windows.
- 504s observed when upstream request takes >10s and gateway times out.
- Customer experiencing user-visible timeouts on conversational retries.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant on us-east-1.
- Serving runtime version: v1.18.3 (post-rollout).
- Cache service: prefix-kv v2.4.0 backed by in-cluster Redis cluster.

Initial hypothesis: a cache revalidation path introduced in the recent serving-runtime change is serializing prefix KV loads for sessions that issue repeated prompts in quick succession, causing amplified cold-load effects and temporary cache contention across worker threads.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a multi-turn conversation where the client sends similar prompts repeatedly (repeat question with small edits) at ~200ms interval.
2) Observe token emission latency and overall request completion time for the 2nd and subsequent turns in sequence.
3) Compare against baseline traffic prior to v1.18.3 rollout or on staging cluster with v1.17.x.
4) Trigger traffic with session affinity to force same KV prefix across parallel requests.

comments: 2026-03-10 09:45 - Aisha Patel (Support): Opened ticket after NimbusChat escalation. Attached traces and Datadog heatmap. Asked SRE to validate if cache revalidation was enabled during the recent rollout.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Diego Martinez (SRE): Confirmed spike windows match deployment of serving-runtime v1.18.3. Noted high number of 'blocking-reval' events in tracer. Asked to collect stack traces from affected pods.
2026-03-10 11:20 - NimbusChat (Customer): Provided sample session IDs and pointed out that repeat prompts are user-driven during editing flows. They can throttle but need platform behavior fixed.

2026-03-11 02:12 - Infra (Eng): Found PR #1592 added synchronous prefix revalidation when TTL is stale; this causes per-session locks. Proposed temporary rollback of that change for dedicated tenants.
2026-03-11 08:33 - Diego Martinez (SRE): Rolled back v1.18.3 to v1.18.1 for NimbusChat dedicated pool. Observed p99 drop back towards baseline within ~5 minutes. Asked Support to confirm customer UX.
2026-03-11 09:10 - NimbusChat (Customer): Confirmed latency improvement after rollback; no 504s observed in the following hour. Requested root cause details and a permanent fix timeline.

2026-03-12 14:55 - Diego Martinez (SRE): Added follow-up: implement asynchronous revalidation with background refresh and per-shard token buckets to avoid thundering revalidations. Planned rollout in v1.19.0.

2026-03-12 15:30 - Aisha Patel (Support): Communicated RCA and workaround to NimbusChat; agreed on testing plan for v1.19.0 canary. Customer asked for postmortem and SLA credit evaluation; support will route to finance after engineering sign-off.
investigation_notes: Traces show sequential requests for same session waiting on a 'revalidation' lock for the same KV prefix (mutex acquired per-prefix).
Cache TTLs were set low for session prefixes (30s) and the revalidation path does a synchronous fetch+index which takes ~1.8-2.2s when cache cold under load.
Because user edits send quick successive requests, multiple workers contend on the same prefix lock causing serialized fetches instead of parallel short reads, amplifying the cold-hit latency.
Redis metrics indicate burst of MGETs and transient CPU spikes on cache nodes during incidents.
resolution: Immediate mitigation: rolled back serving-runtime v1.18.3 to previous stable (v1.18.1) for the affected dedicated pool; observed p99 latency improvement within minutes.
Short-term workaround: disabled synchronous revalidation flag for dedicated tenants and increased prefix cache TTLs to 120s to reduce revalidation frequency.

Long-term fix: scheduled change in serving-runtime to make revalidation async with a background refresh, introduce per-prefix in-flight suppression (singleflight) and add jittered backoff to avoid thundering revalidations. Target release: v1.19.0.
Post-incident actions: add unit + integration tests that simulate rapid conversational turns, add canary for dedicated pools, update runbook with detection queries and rollback steps.
Owner for follow-ups: Diego Martinez (SRE) and Priya Rao (Runtime Eng).
next_steps: 1) Engineering to land async revalidation patch and singleflight logic in PR referenced above (target v1.19.0).
2) QA to create a stress test simulating repeated prompts at 50-300ms intervals across session affinity.
3) Support to prepare customer-facing postmortem and confirm SLA remediation path with finance/legal.
4) Monitor canary for 72 hours after v1.19.0 rollout with dashboard alerts for blocking-reval events and p99 latency regression.
